item.title: BYD combines solar arrays, energy storage and megawatt charging
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: BYD has unveiled a charging system in the Abu Dhabi desert that combines photovoltaics, battery storage, FLASH Charging, and a charging robot. According to CarNewsChina, the system achieved a charging power of 1,000 kW during a demonstration.

item.title: Mercedes discontinues EQE, EQE SUV and EQS SUV
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: The EQE sedan, EQE SUV, and EQS SUV are no longer individually configurable at Mercedes-Benz. This leaves only the EQS sedan remaining from the four large electric models based on the EVA-II platform, while a fully electric E-Class as an EQE alternative has already been announced for 2027.

item.title: California reopens $55m funding programme for electric school buses
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: California has reopened its Zero-Emission School Bus and Infrastructure (ZESBI) incentive programme, with at least $55 million in state funding available to help school districts purchase electric school buses and install the associated charging infrastrcture.

item.title: India: ChargeZone announces 1,000 new DC fast-charging sites
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Indian EV charging service provider ChargeZone has announced plans to deploy DC fast chargers across 1,000 new locations in the country. The company says these chargers will serve both passenger and commercial electric vehicles.

item.title: Zenobe to finance 169 electric buses for Transport UK in London
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Zenobē has agreed to finance 169 battery-electric buses for Transport UK, alongside the development of charging infrastructure at four of the operator's London depots. The deal extends an existing partnership between the two companies and supports Transport UK's ambition to fully electrify its London bus fleet by 2030.

item.title: Infineon processes SiC on 300 mm wafers for the first time
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Infineon has produced the first functional SiC power devices on 300-millimeter wafers. The larger wafer diameter is intended to make production more efficient and, in the long term, improve supply for applications including EVs and charging infrastructure.

item.title: Faulty software? Waymo faces potential new recall
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The US traffic safety authority NHTSA has launched a new investigation into Alphabet's subsidiary Waymo after its driverless taxis repeatedly passed stopped school buses in violation of regulations. An investigation is now exploring why a software update rolled out at the end of 2025 failed to prevent these dangerous violations.

item.title: Kia reveals UK prices for PV5 Chassis and high-roof electric van
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Two new additions to Kia's PV5 electric van range, the Chassis and the high-roof Cargo L2/H2, are expected to be available from £25,605 and £27,355 respectively - once they qualify for the UK's Zero Emission Van Grant (ZEVG). Both models are now available to order, with first deliveries of the Chassis expected in Q1 2027.

item.title: Xpeng launches range-extender SUVs in 11 Middle Eastern and African markets
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Xpeng has opened pre-orders for its flagship GX and G9L SUVs in 11 countries across the MEA region. The two models are being introduced in a shared launch across ten markets, with the GX also launching in Egypt and the G9L in Ghana.

item.title: Pulsa to open private wallboxes for EV drivers
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: With Pulsa, private wallboxes can be temporarily made accessible to other EV drivers. Three weeks after its launch, the platform has reported 250 registrations.

item.title: Volvo Penta and Ammann develop all-electric road paver
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Swiss construction machinery manufacturer Ammann, together with drive specialist Volvo Penta, has developed a fully electric road paver. The eABG 4820 is designed to combine the performance of conventional diesel machines with locally emission-free operation.

media:content.media:description: Auf YouTube findest du die angesagtesten Videos und Tracks. Außerdem kannst du eigene Inhalte hochladen und mit Freunden oder gleich der ganzen Welt teilen.

item.title: CATL explores lithium-air batteries as a long-term research focus
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: CATL is considering lithium-air batteries as a long-term research option. The technology theoretically promises a significantly higher energy density than today's lithium-ion batteries. However, it is still far from market-ready vehicle batteries or a range of 2,000 km.

item.title: Polestar’s design strategy: Formula 2030 showcar sets the direction
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Polestar unveils the Formula 2030 concept car, showcasing the brand's future design direction. Formula 2030 is the first study under the leadership of Chief Designer Philipp Römers, who took up the position in mid-2024. As a four-door sports car, the show car is intended to emphasize that performance remains at the heart of the brand.

item.title: BYD considers building a battery factory in Portugal
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: BYD is reportedly considering building a battery factory in Portugal - potentially at the former Galp refinery in Matosinhos near Porto. It remains unclear whether battery cells or complete battery systems would be manufactured there. Such a battery factory would align well with a potential BYD car factory in Spain.

item.title: VW hints at SSP model production at Martorell Seat plant
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: In an internal report on future collective bargaining strategy, Volkswagen has also indicated that it will "probably assign a platform and products" to the Seat plant in Martorell (Spain). This could refer to the SSP, which will underpin the electric successors to the Cupra Leon and Formentor.

item.title: Mercedes eCitaro to switch to a dedicated electric platform from 2028
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Daimler Buses has announced the second generation eCitaro. From 2028, the electric city bus will be based on a dedicated electric platform, utilise LFP batteries – and even handle some intercity routes. We attended the presentation of the near-series prototype in Munich.

item.title: Chargebyte launches more robust control unit for megawatt charging stations
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: With the new Charge Control Y, Chargebyte now offers a high-load charging controller for megawatt charging in heavy-duty transport. The IP65-protected control unit is designed to reliably protect charging stations in depots, ports, and logistics centers from extreme weather and high-voltage faults.

item.title: Renault opens UK pre-orders for Trafic E-Tech electric from £38,000
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: UK customers can now place pre-orders for the new Trafic E-Tech electric van, which was first presented by Renault in November 2025. Prices start from £38,000 ex. VAT, with the first customer deliveries scheduled for Q2 of 2027.

item.title: Perth’s largest electric bus depot opens as Transperth fleet surpasses 200 vehicles
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Western Australia's largest electric bus depot has opened in Bayswater, Perth. The new facility is equipped with 65 dual chargers and two single chargers, and can initially accommodate 132 electric buses - with scope for up to 180 long term.

item.title: Greenspot and Kempower to build 30 fast-charging sites in France
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Greenspot plans to install Kempower fast-charging infrastructure at 30 retail locations in France by the end of 2027. Each site will feature four charging points powered by a central 200 kW unit.

item.title: Wien Energie expands charging network across Austria following Ella acquisition
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Following the acquisition of Ella GmbH & Co KG, Austrian energy provider Wien Energie has now fully taken over 500 publicly accessible charging points in Lower Austria, Upper Austria, and Burgenland - and, following a multi-month transition phase, integrated them into its charging network.

item.title: Norway: Ionity halts Ekoenergetyka pilot – and installs Huawei chargers for first time
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: At the end of 2025, Ionity opened its first charging park in Elverum, Norway - which features the so-called Shared Power technology by Ekoenergetyka. However, the pilot failed. Since then, Ionity has removed the charging stations and replaced them with new ones from Huawei. It marks the first time that Ionity will work with Huawei.

item.title: Egypt’s first electric car: Dongfeng Mage EV rolls off the production line
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Egypt has launched production of its first locally manufactured electric car, marking the beginning of a new e-mobility offensive. The Dongfeng Mage EV is being built in the state-owned El Nasr Automotive workshops. Egypt aims to produce up to 100,000 electric vehicles annually by 2032.

item.title: 60 driverless electric haul trucks operating at 5,400 metres above sea level
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: In China’s Zhibula copper mine, 60 battery-electric dump trucks are now operating fully autonomously at an altitude of over 5,400 meters. EACON Mining and Julong Copper have gradually introduced driverless operations since 2025, achieving what they claim is a unique deployment in high-altitude mining.

item.title: BMW to source battery cells from LGES and Samsung SDI
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: BMW is expanding its regional network for battery cell supply. For the Gen6 batteries of the Neue Klasse, two additional suppliers, Samsung SDI in Europe and LG Energy Solution (LGES) in the USA, are coming onboard as the automaker aims to further regionalise its supply chains and secure supply.

item.title: Yangwang’s electric chauffeur limousine: the Altior’s luxury offering
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: BYD's Yangwang brand presents the Altior - a luxury sedan primarily designed for the Chinese market and the Middle East. This extraordinary electric vehicle, with a length of 5.60 meters, surpasses almost all luxury cars available in the region. Accordingly, the interior and equipment are generously designed.

item.title: Used EV batteries marketplace Rebattex partners with LKQ Atracco
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Nordic companies Rebattex and LKQ Atracco plan to collaborate in the battery circular economy. Specifically, they intend to offer refurbished EV batteries from LKQ Atracco's locations in Sweden and Norway for sale via the Rebattex platform.

item.title: Posco Future M to supply 720,000 tonnes of battery materials to LG Energy Solution
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Posco Future M and LG Energy Solution are significantly expanding their collaboration on battery materials. Between 2027 and 2033, Posco Future M is set to supply a total of 720,000 tonnes of cathode and anode materials.

item.title: Dacia weighs up European launch for India-only Renault Bridger
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Dacia could be set to expand its range of electric cars in Europe with another model. According to reports, the Renault subsidiary is considering bringing the Renault Bridger, developed for the Indian market, to Europe as an electric car - for which it would need to be adapted accordingly.

item.title: BMW to partially use LFP batteries in Neue Klasse
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: BMW CEO Milan Nedeljković has confirmed that the Neue Klasse electric vehicles will use both NMC and LFP batteries - but very selectively. In China, the iX3 30L already uses an LFP battery, while the more expensive 40L and 50L versions continue to rely on NMC chemistry.
